title: The conditional
why: Built on the future stem, the conditional finally lets the learner ask politely (¿Podrías…? ¿Te importaría…?), express wishes (me gustaría) and give advice (deberías, yo que tú). The lesson keeps to these everyday uses, without if-clauses, and prepares the invitations of the next lesson.

{"lessons": ["

The conditional: future stem + -ía

The conditional is the Spanish \"would.\" It uses the same stem as the future (the infinitive) and adds the imperfect endings of -er and -ir verbs: -ía, -ías, -ía… So hablaría = I would speak, in a single word.

hablarcomervivir
yohablaríacomeríaviviría
túhablaríascomeríasvivirías
él, ella, ustedhablaríacomeríaviviría
nosotros, nosotrashablaríamoscomeríamosviviríamos
vosotros, vosotrashablaríaiscomeríaisviviríais
ellos, ellas, ustedeshablaríancomeríanvivirían

The written accent is on the í, in every person.

Irregular verbs: exactly the same as the future

InfinitiveFutureConditionalEnglish
tenertendrétendríaI'd have
salirsaldrésaldríaI'd go out
venirvendrévendríaI'd come
ponerpondrépondríaI'd put
poderpodrépodríaI could
sabersabrésabríaI'd know
quererquerréquerríaI'd want
hacerharéharíaI'd do, I'd make
decirdirédiríaI'd say
haber (hay)habráhabríathere would be

Don't mix it up with the imperfect: comía (I was eating, I used to eat) / comería (I would eat). The conditional keeps the whole infinitive: comería. Careful with English \"would\" meaning \"used to\" (\"as a kid, I would eat there every Sunday\"): that's the imperfect in Spanish, not the conditional!

", "

Asking politely and saying what you'd like

You already know quería and ¿podría…? as set phrases. Here's the whole system:

To…SentenceTranslation
ask a friend for a favor¿Podrías ayudarme con la maleta?Could you help me with my suitcase?
ask formally (usted)¿Podría decirme la hora?Could you tell me the time?
ask very gently¿Te importaría cerrar la ventana?Would you mind closing the window?
express a wishMe gustaría aprender a bailar.I'd like to learn to dance.
a very strong wishMe encantaría vivir en Barcelona.I'd love to live in Barcelona.
a preferencePreferiría quedarme en casa.I'd rather stay home.

Me gustaría: works like gustar

Gustar and encantar keep their usual construction: me gustaría, te gustaría, le gustaría, nos gustaría, os gustaría, les gustaría. With an infinitive, the verb stays singular: A mis padres les gustaría viajar. With a plural noun, it becomes plural: Me gustarían unas vacaciones tranquilas.

When you answer ¿Te importaría…?, careful: No, para nada or Claro que no mean \"no, I don't mind at all,\" so it's actually a yes! Exactly like English: \"Would you mind? — No, not at all.\"

", "

Giving advice

PhraseExampleTranslation
deberías + infinitiveDeberías descansar más.You should rest more.
tendrías que + infinitiveTendrías que ir al médico.You ought to see a doctor.
yo que tú + conditionalYo que tú, hablaría con ella.If I were you, I'd talk to her.
yo en tu lugar + conditionalYo en tu lugar, no diría nada.In your place, I wouldn't say anything.
sería mejor + infinitiveSería mejor salir temprano.It would be better to leave early.

Yo que tú is the most typical expression of spoken Spanish: word for word \"I that you,\" meaning \"if I were you.\" With usted: Yo que usted, cogería un taxi.

Deberías is softer than debes (you must), exactly like \"you should\" is softer than \"you must.\"

Estás agobiada: yo que tú, me tomaría unos días de vacaciones.You're swamped: if I were you, I'd take a few days off.

As in English, the conditional also shows up in sentences with \"if\" (\"if I had time, I would travel\"). But after si, Spanish uses another tense you'll learn later: for now, keep the conditional for politeness, advice and wishes.
